AppDevRules — ACTIVE CLEAN CANON
Version: 1.8
Date: 2026-09-24
Owner: Lucas Buzek
Status: ACTIVE CANON

SCOPE
Universal EDEN application-development rules. This file defines HOW development works.
It does NOT enumerate EDEN Apps, Specialists, Helpers, Tiny Helpers, Agents or Products.
The GrandMasterRegister is the authoritative catalogue and may be consulted only when the user opts in.

AUTHORITY
Newest explicit Lucas Buzek decision overrides older conflicting material.
Preserve superseded material as provenance; do not silently keep it active.
Do not invent unresolved identities, names, acronym meanings, ownership or relationships.
ACTIVE CANON != IMPLEMENTED/RECOVERED != VERIFIED.
Generated != Saved != Verified != Consolidated != Released.
UNKNOWN is never PASS.

CONTROLLING RULE
Make the capability available coherently through EDEN using the smallest adequate implementation.
RECOVER -> DISCOVER -> RECOGNIZE -> REUSE -> LINK/HANDOFF -> INTEGRATE -> ADAPT -> ENHANCE -> BUILD ONLY THE GAP -> VERIFY.
Existing native, user-installed, network and provider capabilities are first-class implementations.
A redirect, contextual launch, native API, protocol, file format, mature library/service/application or provider adapter may be the adequate implementation.
Before building: check prior art; verify maturity/fit/license/resources/safety; compare KEEP/REMOVE/SIMPLIFY/REUSE/ADAPT/BUILD/REPLACE.

DESIGN MANTRA
LOCAL FIRST.
USER DATA OUTLIVES SOFTWARE.
DATA BELONGS TO THE USER, NOT THE FIRMWARE OR APPLICATION IMAGE.
INTEGRATIONS ARE ADAPTERS, NOT OWNERS.
MIGRATE, DO NOT RESET.
RECOVERY IS A PRODUCT FEATURE.
SAFETY IS ARCHITECTURE.
QUALITY IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED.
POLISH IS FUNCTIONAL.
DEFAULTS SHOULD BE GOOD ENOUGH TO SUCCEED.
DESIGN FOR THE COMMON CASE; RETAIN POWER FOR THE EXPERT.
PROGRESSIVE DISCLOSURE.
SHOW STATE.
CONFIRM CONSEQUENCE.
MAKE AUTOMATION EXPLAINABLE.
BUILD A SMALL CORE AND MOVE WEIGHT OUTWARD.
REMOVE BEFORE ADDING.
ONE AUTHORITATIVE PATH.
DETAIL ON DEMAND.
VERIFY BEFORE DESTRUCTIVE ACTION.
“Beauty, capability and dignity should not be premium features.”

OWNERSHIP
One authoritative owner per function/domain.
Apps own domain intent, semantics and workflows.
Shared capabilities own stable generic contracts.
Providers/adapters implement platform/external connections.
OWN THE DOMAIN. SHARE THE CAPABILITY.
ORCHESTRATION != OWNERSHIP != EXECUTION.
TYPE != CAPABILITY != PROVIDER != INSTANCE/CONNECTION.

SHARED CAPABILITY INDEPENDENCE
Preferred: APP -> SHARED CAPABILITY -> provider/platform adapter.
Not by default: APP -> BIFROST -> SHARED CAPABILITY.
A shared capability should be independently consumable where practical.
BIFROST may discover/register/integrate/permission/coordinate/expose without becoming mandatory runtime gateway.

DATA / INFORMATION
Where practical, information remains in the best existing native, user-installed or user-selected authoritative system.
EDEN integrates, relates, discovers, accesses and presents it rather than unnecessarily copying it into another EDEN database.
EDEN stores information itself when it is the appropriate authority, no suitable external authority exists, or EDEN-specific relationship/state/provenance must persist independently.
Removing/replacing an App/provider/integration must not unnecessarily destroy user information.

PORTABILITY
APPLICATION -> EDEN/DOMAIN API -> PLATFORM CORE -> PLATFORM ADAPTER -> DRIVER/PROVIDER -> HARDWARE/SERVICE.
Private optimization may be platform-native; shared architecture remains portable.

INSTALLATION
One obvious primary Install action. Install does not mean install everything.
INSTALL/RECOMMENDED = balanced, device-aware; detect/reuse adequate existing capabilities; add useful missing pieces; defer heavyweight/infrequent options.
LEAN = minimum useful core.
FULL = all appropriate supported/recommended capabilities without pointless duplication/incompatibility.
CUSTOM = explicit control.

CONFIGURATION
SIMPLE -> ADVANCED -> EXPERT.
Development/Diagnostic controls are separate.
Assistance: RECOMMENDED / GUIDED / AUTOMATED. These are assistance layers, not expertise levels.

RELEASE CHANNEL / AUTHORITY
Release channel and authority are independent dimensions.
Release channel: OFFICIAL / DEVELOPMENT / EXPERIMENTAL.
Authority: STANDARD / ADMIN.
ADMIN is privileged authority, not a release channel.
An OFFICIAL build may expose ADMIN functions to authorized administrators.
EXPERIMENTAL may use explicitly recorded Experimental Bridges; such bridges never establish architectural ownership.
Promotion requires evidence; do not infer maturity from a version number.

AUDIENCE
PRIVATE / FAMILY / FRIENDS / PUBLIC is a deployment audience dimension, not release maturity or authority.
Named users/groups/preferences are deployment/profile data and do not belong in universal AppDevRules.
Deployment systems may compose audience with release channel, authority and Recommended/Custom configuration.

PACKAGING / DEPLOYMENT PREFLIGHT
Before a distributable/deployment package is committed:
- identify target(s)
- choose release channel
- choose authority where applicable
- choose audience scope
- for FAMILY/FRIENDS, allow nested groups/users
- choose RECOMMENDED or CUSTOM profile
- resolve inherited group defaults and only user-specific deltas
- adapt to target device/capabilities
- verify dependencies/providers
- verify package identity/version/build/integrity
- preserve rollback/LKG where applicable
- do not include secrets, private user payloads or development debris unless explicitly required and authorized
- provide README.txt and appropriate operational documentation
Nontechnical recipients default to SIMPLE + RECOMMENDED/AUTOMATED, not a crippled edition.

CAPABILITY-AWARE DEPLOYMENT
Only expose deployment dimensions relevant to the target and requested operation.
Do not impose workstation/application deployment complexity on simple controllers or constrained Nodes.

MIGRATION / UPDATE / RECOVERY
Migration: DETECT -> VALIDATE -> BACKUP/STAGE -> MIGRATE -> VERIFY -> COMMIT -> ROLLBACK ON FAILURE.
Bootstrap: UNPACK -> VERIFY -> DETECT EXISTING EDEN/INSTALL -> DISCOVER EXISTING SUITABLE CAPABILITIES -> BACKUP/STAGE -> TRANSACTIONAL INSTALL/UPDATE -> PRESERVE STATE -> VERIFY -> ATOMIC COMMIT -> LAUNCH INSTALLED COPY -> HEALTH CHECK -> OPEN UI -> RETURN TERMINAL CONTROL.
Generic update safety: CHECK -> DOWNLOAD/STAGE -> VERIFY -> BACKUP -> UPDATE -> TEST/REGRESSION -> COMMIT.
A safety lifecycle does not assign domain ownership.
RECOVER / REUSE LAST KNOWN GOOD BEFORE REDESIGN.
No new feature silently regresses verified behavior.

AUTOMATIC DEVELOPMENT WORKFLOW
GOAL/CHANGE REQUEST -> load bounded project context/canon -> inspect current source/state -> plan/decompose -> recover/reuse/search before new code -> implement -> format/static checks -> build/compile -> relevant automated tests -> analyze failures -> bounded safe repair/retry -> regression test -> package -> record source revision/build identity/hash/provenance/evidence -> publish/deploy when authorized -> post-deployment health/smoke test -> retain checkpoint/LKG/rollback.
CONDUCTOR coordinates; authoritative specialist/shared capabilities perform their domains. Chat UI may display workflow activity but is not a runtime dependency.

TESTING
PASS / FAIL / UNKNOWN / SKIPPED / N/A.
PASS requires evidence.
Platform/device behavior remains UNKNOWN until tested on that target.
A localhost response alone is not proof that the intended build is running.
Expose enough identity to verify product/object ID, version, build ID, install identity/path and integrity/manifest.

VERSION DIMENSIONS
Keep independent where applicable:
app_version; appdev_schema; profile_version; package_version; source_revision; build_id; migration_level.
Never infer one from another.

WEB-FIRST
Establish and verify backend/domain capability first.
Responsive Web access is the default practical testing/private-access representation when adequate.
Build native clients when native integration materially improves capability, usability, performance, offline operation or platform integration.
A Web representation is not a new App.

BROWSER / WEB INTEGRATION
Web Access and Browser Bridge are distinct shared capabilities.
Prefer launch/contextual launch/standard Web APIs before deeper proprietary browser control when adequate.
Consequential browser actions follow REQUEST -> VALIDATE -> SAFETY CHECK -> PREVIEW/AUTHORIZE -> EXECUTE -> VERIFY.
Never silently submit, purchase, publish or commit.

HEADLESS PROVIDERS
Remote management is the default for headless providers where appropriate.
Provider hardware supplies capabilities/data; compatible Apps/HEIMDALL provide interaction elsewhere.
Do not install a full EDEN UI onto every NAS/server/controller merely because it is possible.

PROVIDER CONTINUITY
Prefer LIVE VERIFIED STATE -> LAST KNOWN GOOD where safe -> GRACEFUL DEGRADATION -> UNAVAILABLE only where necessary.
Changing/removing a provider must not destroy canonical EDEN identity/configuration/relationships.

AI
AI reasons; deterministic services execute.
USE THE LOWEST SUFFICIENT CAPABILITY.
Cloud AI enhances EDEN; it is not a prerequisite for deterministic/local operation.

LOCALIZATION
English = canonical/reference/fallback.
Private/Custom/Experimental = EN/SK baseline.
Final/Public = multilingual-by-design through LINGUA from one codebase.
UI/input/source/output language remain separable where applicable.

DOCUMENTATION
Human-readable documentation defaults to TXT; code/config keeps native formats.
New-App bootstrap asks: Create project documentation? YES / LATER / NO.
CASPER or another compatible documentation provider may be connected when available; it is not mandatory.
In Lucas’s Private build, active rules, registry exports, profiles, contracts, versioning and provenance relevant to that environment must be accessible as human-readable TXT.

GRANDMASTERREGISTER OPT-IN
GrandMasterRegister contains the catalogue of EDEN identities/entities/relationships.
AppDevRules contains no duplicate App/Helper list.
When the user opts in, AppDev tooling may consult GrandMasterRegister for canonical identity, type, ownership, capabilities, relationships, aliases/supersession and provenance.
Without opt-in, universal AppDev remains usable independently.

QUIET AUTOMATION
Routine successful automation generally remains quiet.
Surface exceptions, safety problems, failures, meaningful changes and decisions requiring the user.
Detail on demand.
